channel_dna.platform_type: Professional social network. Dominant for B2B, enterprise, career, and business content. World's largest professional community.
channel_dna.algorithm_type: Social graph + interest graph hybrid. Early engagement from your network (first 1-2 hrs) determines wider distribution. 'Dwell time' (how long people read) is a key signal. Content stays active 24-72 hours. Comments from your connections in the first hour are the single biggest algorithmic lever.
channel_dna.primary_audience: Professionals aged 25-55. Decision-makers, managers, founders, sales and marketing professionals. 65% B2B decision-makers use LinkedIn for research. Average HHI is significantly higher than other platforms.
channel_dna.native_content_formats: Long-form text posts (1300 chars performs best), carousels (PDF documents), short videos (under 3 min), articles, polls, newsletters. Text posts with no images get highest organic reach counterintuitively.
channel_dna.platform_culture_code: Professional but increasingly personal. Vulnerability and personal stories perform well. Data-driven insights respected. Thought leadership over self-promotion. Comments are heavily weighted — the platform rewards conversation starters. Unlike Twitter, LinkedIn rewards depth and dwell time over speed and virality.
channel_dna.account_warmup_requirements: Profile must be 100% complete with professional photo. 500+ connections baseline for credibility. Creator Mode enabled to get Follow button. First 90 days: engage in comment sections daily before posting original content, connect strategically with ICP, optimise profile headline.

profile_setup.step_1_profile_photo: Use a professional headshot — real face, good lighting, friendly expression. This is LinkedIn, not Twitter — slightly more polished is appropriate. Profile photos with a real face get 21x more views than logos or generic avatars.
profile_setup.step_2_headline: Your headline is the most important copy on your profile. It appears below your name in every comment, reply, and search result. Formula: '[What you do] | Building [Product] | [One-line value prop or audience]'. Example: 'Founder | Building Farcast — AI growth agent for founders | Helping vibe coders get their first 100 users'. Avoid generic titles like 'Entrepreneur' or 'CEO at [Company]' with no context.
profile_setup.step_3_about_section: Write the About section in first person, conversational tone. Tell your story: what you were doing before, what problem you noticed, what you are building and why. End with a clear CTA: 'Follow me for weekly posts on [topic area]' or 'If you are building a product and stuck on distribution, DM me.'
profile_setup.step_4_featured_section: Use the Featured section to pin your product URL, a recent post that performed well, or a relevant piece of content. This is permanent and visible — treat it as a landing page.
profile_setup.step_5_creator_mode: Turn on Creator Mode in Settings. This changes your profile from 'Connect' to 'Follow' as the primary button, adds your content topics below your headline, and gives you access to LinkedIn Newsletter and LinkedIn Live.
profile_setup.step_6_connection_strategy: Connect with 10-20 targeted people per day: founders in adjacent spaces, potential ICP members (by job title search), journalists in your niche, operators at companies your ICP works at. Always add a personalised connection note referencing something specific.

fit_scoring_matrix.best_product_types: B2B SaaS, HR tech, sales tools, marketing tools, enterprise software, professional services, recruiting tools, finance tools, productivity for teams
fit_scoring_matrix.worst_product_types: B2C consumer apps (especially for under-25 audience), gaming, consumer entertainment, anything lifestyle-focused, student tools
fit_scoring_matrix.best_pricing_models: Paid and freemium both work well. LinkedIn audience has purchasing authority and budget. Paid products with clear ROI narrative convert well.
fit_scoring_matrix.icp_match_signals: Search your ICP job title on LinkedIn — if 1M+ people have that title, the audience is there. Check if there are active LinkedIn Groups in your category with 10K+ members.
fit_scoring_matrix.red_flags_skip_this_channel: Skip if target users are under 25 (students, Gen Z consumers). Skip if your product has no professional/business use case. Skip if your ICP is non-English speaking markets where LinkedIn penetration is low.
fit_scoring_matrix.geographic_strength: US (185M users), India (107M), Brazil (65M), UK (38M), Canada (21M). Strong in English-speaking professional markets globally.

growth_mechanics.expected_cac: $0 for organic. LinkedIn Ads are expensive ($5-15 CPC) but highly targeted. Organic content is the primary acquisition play for early-stage.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_traffic_spike: 3-6 weeks of consistent posting before meaningful traction. LinkedIn has a slower build than Twitter but more durable engagement.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_paying_user: 4-8 weeks for B2B products with a defined outreach strategy. LinkedIn is a pipeline builder, not an impulse conversion channel.
growth_mechanics.effort_level: Medium-High. 3-4 posts per week. Daily commenting on target accounts is as important as posting. Profile maintenance and strategic connecting takes consistent effort.
growth_mechanics.virality_coefficient: Low-Medium. Content spreads through professional networks. Viral posts typically reach 10K-100K impressions. Rarely becomes truly viral like Twitter or TikTok.
growth_mechanics.compounding_potential: Medium-High. Followers compound slowly but stickily. Newsletter subscribers compound well. Published articles have long-term SEO value.

algorithm_playbook.how_reach_is_determined: Engagement in first 60-90 minutes from your immediate connections. Dwell time (people stopping to read). Comments weighted 4x more than likes. Comment replies from the author boost post further. Early comments from high-follower accounts amplify significantly.
algorithm_playbook.what_algorithm_rewards: Posts that generate conversation (multiple comment threads). Posts people save. Native documents (carousels) because they increase dwell time. Personal stories that generate emotional responses. Consistency — posting 3-4x/week trains the algorithm. Author replies to comments in the first hour.
algorithm_playbook.what_kills_reach: External links in post body (LinkedIn suppresses these — always put links in first comment). More than 3 hashtags. Tagging many people who don't engage (spam signal). Posting and not responding to comments. Cross-posting from other platforms without reformatting.
algorithm_playbook.peak_posting_windows: Tuesday-Thursday 7:30-8:30am local time (commute window). Tuesday 10am-12pm. Wednesday 8-10am. Avoid weekends — LinkedIn engagement drops 40%.
algorithm_playbook.optimal_posting_cadence: 3-4 posts per week maximum. Daily posting beyond 5x/week triggers algorithmic suppression. Comment on 10-20 posts from your ICP daily — this is as important as original posting.
algorithm_playbook.content_freshness_window: Posts stay active 24-72 hours depending on engagement velocity. Unlike Twitter, LinkedIn content can resurface days later if it receives a comment spike.

execution_sequence.phase_1_comment_engagement: For the first 2-4 weeks, make commenting your primary activity. Find 10-20 accounts your ICP follows or that your ICP type posts on. Every day, leave 10-15 substantive comments on their posts. Comments must add genuine value — share a related insight, a personal experience, a data point, or a respectful alternative perspective. Never 'Great post!' — it is algorithmically invisible and personally forgettable.
execution_sequence.phase_2_original_posting: Begin posting 3-4x per week. Keep the comment-to-post ratio high — for every post you write, leave 10 comments on others. Do not stop commenting when you start posting. The two activities compound each other: your comments drive profile visits, your posts convert those visitors.
execution_sequence.phase_3_consistent_mix: Mature cadence: daily commenting (10-20 posts), 3-4 original posts per week, 1 carousel/document every 2 weeks, strategic connection requests to ICP daily. Reply to every comment on your own posts within 2 hours — this is the biggest single lever for algorithmic reach.

content_system.winning_content_types: 1. Personal story with a professional lesson — what happened, what you learned, what you'd do differently 2. Data-driven insight from your own product or experience 3. Founder journey update with real numbers — transparent milestones 4. Carousel/document — step-by-step guides or frameworks with visual slides 5. Contrarian take on conventional wisdom in your space 6. 'What I wish I knew when I started [X]' format
content_system.hook_formulas: Specific number: 'I sent 500 cold emails last month. Here is what I learned.' | Bold statement: 'Most startup founders waste their first 6 months on the wrong thing.' | Personal failure: 'I almost shut down my company last year. Here is what saved it.' | Curiosity gap: 'The single post that got me 50 inbound leads (and what made it work).'
content_system.platform_native_tone: Professional but human. First-person. Honest about failures. Data-backed claims. Paragraphs are short (1-2 sentences for readability). No jargon. No corporate buzzwords. The best LinkedIn posts sound like a smart colleague talking at a coffee meeting — not a press release.
content_system.personalisation_layer: LinkedIn rewards specificity even more than Twitter because the audience is professional and skeptical. Generic 'here are 5 tips for founders' posts are everywhere. Posts that reference a real conversation you had this week, a decision your team made yesterday, or a specific number from your product perform dramatically better. Always ask: 'Is there a real moment from my week that makes this point more concrete?'
content_system.cta_approach: Single CTA at end of post. Options: 'Comment your experience below', 'Link to full resource in comments' (never in post body — LinkedIn suppresses), 'DM me if you want to chat about X'. Product mentions should be organic and contextual, never the lead.
content_system.content_to_avoid: Engagement bait ('Comment YES if you agree'). Corporate press release tone. Excessive hashtag use (1-2 max). Humble-bragging without substance. Posting the same content repeatedly. 'Inspirational' quotes with no original insight. Anything that reads like an ad.
content_system.cross_posting_rules: Twitter threads need heavy expansion for LinkedIn — add context, depth, and a more professional frame. TikTok video scripts can work if reformatted as text posts with the casual energy dialled back slightly. Never auto-cross-post without rewriting.

community_outreach_playbook.where_icp_clusters: LinkedIn Groups (search your ICP category), company pages of your ICP's employers, specific job title searches, industry hashtag feeds (#SaaS, #ProductManagement, #B2BSales). LinkedIn Events attract concentrated ICP.
community_outreach_playbook.contribution_before_pitch_rule: Comment genuinely on 10-20 ICP posts every day for the first month. Add insights, share experiences, ask smart follow-up questions. Become a recognisable name in their feed before you ever reach out. People check the profile of commenters who add genuine value — your profile should convert those visits.
community_outreach_playbook.dm_outreach_approach: InMail for non-connections — personalise every single message. Reference something specific they posted. Keep under 3 sentences. Never pitch in first message — ask a question or give value. Connection request: always add a personalised note. Response rates 3-5x higher with personalisation vs. generic 'I'd like to connect'.
community_outreach_playbook.influencer_partner_strategy: LinkedIn newsletter collaborations are powerful — cross-promote with complementary newsletters. Target thought leaders with 10K-100K followers for co-written posts. LinkedIn Live collaborations also drive mutual audience growth.
community_outreach_playbook.broadcast_vs_community_mode: Both, with commenting as the primary community mechanism. Build an audience through posts, convert through DMs and comments. LinkedIn is a pipeline tool — use it to start conversations, not close deals.
community_outreach_playbook.banned_behaviours: Mass connection requests without personalisation (LinkedIn rate-limits and may restrict account). Automated messaging tools (against ToS). Posting misleading statistics. Selling in InMail without relationship context. Scraping LinkedIn data.

business_stage_playbook.pre_launch_0_users: Build founder personal brand around the PROBLEM space, not the solution. Share research findings, customer interview insights, market observations. 'I have been talking to 50 [ICP job title] about [problem] and here is what I am learning.' Builds credibility and pre-qualifies audience before you have anything to sell.
business_stage_playbook.early_traction_1_to_100: Share the founding story with real detail. Be transparent about early traction — what is working, what is not. Tag early customers in success posts (with permission). This stage is about converting professional credibility into product curiosity.
business_stage_playbook.growth_100_to_1k: Case studies with real customer names and metrics (requires permission). Industry data posts that position your product category. Begin LinkedIn newsletter for owned audience. Start targeted connection campaigns to your ICP.
business_stage_playbook.scale_1k_plus: LinkedIn Ads for retargeting website visitors. Sponsored content for top-performing organic posts. Employee advocacy program. Company page content strategy separate from founder content.

proof_of_play.early_stage_win: Gong.io — founder Amit Bendov built a LinkedIn following sharing revenue intelligence insights and sales data before the product scaled. Thought leadership content drove inbound pipeline worth millions. He was a prolific commenter on sales and revenue posts before becoming a known voice.
proof_of_play.growth_stage_win: HubSpot — dominated LinkedIn with inbound marketing education content for years before competitors caught on. Built category ownership through consistent educational posting that drove massive organic pipeline.
proof_of_play.what_made_it_work: Both shared genuinely useful industry knowledge that their ICP needed — not product features. Both were visible in comment sections before they were known for original content. The product was naturally positioned as the tool that enabled the outcomes they were teaching about.
proof_of_play.what_would_have_killed_it: A feed full of 'New product update — check out our latest feature' posts would have been ignored by the algorithm and the audience. Pure broadcast without comment engagement would have grown their following at a fraction of the speed.
